elements.element: Transition assistance provided on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Transition assistance duration of up to 6 months
Transition assistance charged at then-current rates
Return in a standard machine-readable format
Return within 30 days of expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "within 30 days of such expiry or termination"

elements.element: Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: "(c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems"
"transition assistance for up to 6 months" exceeds the 90-day floor
"return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days"

reasons: The inserted Section 10.3 supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: 6-month transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format measured from expiry or termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter.

The "at Customer's request" condition attaches only to limb (a) transition assistance, which is inherently elective; the mandatory data-return, deletion, and certification obligations in limbs (b) and (c) are not gated by any request, so the request condition does not swallow post-termination data return.

Minimality holds: the document previously had no exit/data-return mechanic (Section 10.1 merely preserved existing rights and 16.5 deferred Customer Data to other sections), so a single concise new subsection is the least intrusive fix; no existing sentence was rewritten or deleted.
Intent is preserved: refund, Deliverable-delivery, and confidentiality provisions remain untouched, no defined term is created, and "Customer Data" and "Order Form" are used as defined.

Noted in rationale only (not a deviation): the softener "reasonable" before "transition assistance" and the absence of a fix to Section 16.5's cross-reference to a non-existent Section 11 leave minor imprecision, but neither defeats a preferred element.
